ops.html: Problem
ops.src: ## Problem

ops.html: agentsh daemon install writes a service unit that starts the server with a --daemon argument:
ops.src:
`agentsh daemon install` writes a service unit that starts the server with a
`--daemon` argument:

ops.html: • internal/cli/daemon.go:208 — ExecStart=%s server --daemon
ops.src: - `internal/cli/daemon.go:208` — `ExecStart=%s server --daemon`

ops.html: • internal/cli/daemon.go:362 — <string>--daemon</string>
ops.src: - `internal/cli/daemon.go:362` — `<string>--daemon</string>`

ops.html: internal/cli/server.go registers only --config, so cobra rejects the argument and the process exits non-zero before doing any work:
ops.src:
`internal/cli/server.go` registers only `--config`, so cobra rejects the
argument and the process exits non-zero before doing any work:

ops.html:
$ agentsh server --daemon
unknown flag: --daemon
ops.src:
```
$ agentsh server --daemon
unknown flag: --daemon
```

ops.html: Both service managers then restart it forever — systemd via Restart=on-failure, launchd via KeepAlive. The reporter's agentsh.err is three identical unknown flag: --daemon lines and launchctl list shows last exit 1.
ops.src:
Both service managers then restart it forever — systemd via `Restart=on-failure`,
launchd via `KeepAlive`. The reporter's `agentsh.err` is three identical
`unknown flag: --daemon` lines and `launchctl list` shows `last exit 1`.

ops.html: agentsh daemon install is broken end-to-end on both Linux and macOS.
ops.src: `agentsh daemon install` is broken end-to-end on both Linux and macOS.

ops.html: Constraint that shapes the fix
ops.src: ## Constraint that shapes the fix

ops.html: Correcting the templates does not repair an existing installation. The unit file already on disk still carries --daemon, and upgrading the binary does not rewrite it. Every user who has already run agentsh daemon install stays in the restart loop until they manually re-run agentsh daemon install --force.
ops.src:
Correcting the templates does not repair an existing installation. The unit
file already on disk still carries `--daemon`, and upgrading the binary does not
rewrite it. Every user who has already run `agentsh daemon install` stays in the
restart loop until they manually re-run `agentsh daemon install --force`.

ops.html: The fix therefore has to work from both directions: stop emitting the argument, and tolerate it where it has already been written.
ops.src:
The fix therefore has to work from both directions: stop emitting the argument,
and tolerate it where it has already been written.

ops.html: Design
ops.src: ## Design

ops.html: 1. Register --daemon as a hidden, deprecated no-op
ops.src: ### 1. Register `--daemon` as a hidden, deprecated no-op

ops.html: In newServerCmd (internal/cli/server.go):
ops.src: In `newServerCmd` (`internal/cli/server.go`):

ops.html:
cmd.Flags().Bool("daemon", false, "Deprecated: accepted for compatibility, ignored")
_ = cmd.Flags().MarkDeprecated("daemon",
    "the server always runs in the foreground under systemd/launchd; remove it or re-run `agentsh daemon install --force`")
ops.src:
```go
cmd.Flags().Bool("daemon", false, "Deprecated: accepted for compatibility, ignored")
_ = cmd.Flags().MarkDeprecated("daemon",
    "the server always runs in the foreground under systemd/launchd; remove it or re-run `agentsh daemon install --force`")
```

ops.html: A no-op is the semantically correct shim, not a placeholder for unimplemented behavior. systemd Type=simple and launchd both require the supervised process to stay in the foreground — self-daemonizing would break process tracking under either. "Run as a daemon" has no work to do in this context, so there is nothing being stubbed out.
ops.src:
A no-op is the semantically correct shim, not a placeholder for unimplemented
behavior. systemd `Type=simple` and launchd both require the supervised process
to stay in the foreground — self-daemonizing would break process tracking under
either. "Run as a daemon" has no work to do in this context, so there is nothing
being stubbed out.

ops.html: pflag.MarkDeprecated also sets Hidden, keeping the flag out of --help, and prints a one-line notice to stderr on each start. Under launchd that notice lands in ~/Library/Logs/agentsh/agentsh.err, where it tells an operator exactly how to clean up a stale unit.
ops.src:
`pflag.MarkDeprecated` also sets `Hidden`, keeping the flag out of `--help`, and
prints a one-line notice to stderr on each start. Under launchd that notice
lands in `~/Library/Logs/agentsh/agentsh.err`, where it tells an operator
exactly how to clean up a stale unit.

ops.html: 2. Drop --daemon from both templates
ops.src: ### 2. Drop `--daemon` from both templates

ops.html:
-ExecStart=%s server --daemon
+ExecStart=%s server
ops.src:
```diff
-ExecStart=%s server --daemon
+ExecStart=%s server
```

ops.html:
<string>server</string>
-        <string>--daemon</string>
     </array>
ops.src:
```diff
         <string>server</string>
-        <string>--daemon</string>
     </array>
```

ops.html: Newly generated units are clean; the flag survives only as a compatibility accommodation for units already on disk.
ops.src:
Newly generated units are clean; the flag survives only as a compatibility
accommodation for units already on disk.

ops.html: 3. Regression guard
ops.src: ### 3. Regression guard

ops.html: In internal/cli/daemon_test.go, render each template with realistic values, extract the argv the service manager would execute, and dry-parse it against the real root command. No server starts and no port is bound.
ops.src:
In `internal/cli/daemon_test.go`, render each template with realistic values,
extract the argv the service manager would execute, and dry-parse it against the
real root command. No server starts and no port is bound.

ops.html: • argvFromSystemdUnit — take the ExecStart= line, split on whitespace, drop argv[0] (the resolved executable path).
ops.src:
- `argvFromSystemdUnit` — take the `ExecStart=` line, split on whitespace, drop
  `argv[0]` (the resolved executable path).

ops.html: • argvFromLaunchdPlist — take the <string> values inside the ProgramArguments <array>, drop argv[0].
ops.src:
- `argvFromLaunchdPlist` — take the `<string>` values inside the
  `ProgramArguments` `<array>`, drop `argv[0]`.

ops.html: • For each: NewRoot("test").Find(argv) must resolve the subcommand, and ParseFlags on the found command must succeed.
ops.src:
- For each: `NewRoot("test").Find(argv)` must resolve the subcommand, and
  `ParseFlags` on the found command must succeed.

ops.html: This covers the whole failure class rather than this one instance — an unregistered flag, a renamed or removed server subcommand, and a structurally broken ExecStart / ProgramArguments all fail the test. Because the compatibility no-op (section 1) makes --daemon itself parse, ParseFlags succeeding is not sufficient on its own; the guard additionally asserts --daemon is absent from the extracted argv.
ops.src:
This covers the whole failure class rather than this one instance — an
unregistered flag, a renamed or removed `server` subcommand, and a structurally
broken `ExecStart` / `ProgramArguments` all fail the test. Because the
compatibility no-op (section 1) makes `--daemon` itself parse, `ParseFlags`
succeeding is not sufficient on its own; the guard additionally asserts
`--daemon` is absent from the extracted argv.

ops.html: A second, smaller test asserts server --daemon still parses and that the flag is hidden, pinning the compatibility promise from section 1 so a future cleanup cannot silently drop it.
ops.src:
A second, smaller test asserts `server --daemon` still parses and that the flag
is hidden, pinning the compatibility promise from section 1 so a future cleanup
cannot silently drop it.

ops.html: Out of scope
ops.src: ## Out of scope

ops.html: Examined and deliberately left alone:
ops.src: Examined and deliberately left alone:

ops.html: • ProtectSystem=strict in the systemd unit makes /run read-only, which can prevent the unix socket listener from binding. The server already degrades gracefully here, logging unix socket disabled and continuing, so it does not block startup.
ops.src:
- **`ProtectSystem=strict` in the systemd unit** makes `/run` read-only, which
  can prevent the unix socket listener from binding. The server already degrades
  gracefully here, logging `unix socket disabled` and continuing, so it does not
  block startup.

ops.html: • Auto-repairing stale unit files on agentsh daemon install. Unnecessary once the no-op flag exists — stale units simply work.
ops.src:
- **Auto-repairing stale unit files** on `agentsh daemon install`. Unnecessary
  once the no-op flag exists — stale units simply work.
